To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the transcription factor aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR) is activated in neurons after stroke; (b) AhR activation protects neurons from stroke damage; (c) AhR activation increases neuronal expression of neuroprotective genes, including the antiapoptotic gene BCL2; and (d) AhR activation is neuroprotective in a mouse model of stroke.
the aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR) is activated in the setting of ischemic stroke and that AhR activation is neuroprotective in this context.

1) the aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR) is a novel regulator of the ischemic response in the brain, 2) the AhR plays a protective role in ischemic stroke, 3) the AhR is an important regulator of the ischemia-induced inflammatory response, and 4) the AhR regulates the expression of genes that are critical in the pathophysiology of stroke.

the development and application of novel, safe, and effective therapies that will help to reduce the morbidity and mortality from stroke and other neurodegenerative disorders.
the development of novel therapeutic approaches to treat ischemic stroke.
understanding the mechanisms by which ischemic brain injury occurs, and with developing novel therapies for stroke.
